title: Retail POC decision notebook — hosting heuristics and quick tradeoffs
body:
Purpose
---
Working notebook to capture a concise comparison of three practical hosting approaches for a mid-market retail POC (B2C storefront assistant + order summarization). This doc is intentionally lightweight — meant for rapid alignment with product and infra stakeholders, and to feed the demo runbook.

Customer context / constraints
---
- Traffic profile (expected for POC): 1k unique users/day, peak concurrent requests ~40, typical burst windows 5–10 minutes during marketing emails.
- Hard constraints: single-region EU data residency requirement for customer data; PCI scope minimization is preferred (no card-data retention in inference layer).
- SLO target for interactive flows: p95 end-to-end < 500ms for short-chat interactions; p99 < 1.2s for generation tasks up to ~256 tokens.
- Budget: pilot monthly spend target <$6k (infrastructure + Redwood usage) for first 3 months.
- Team: small eng + product; limited ops bandwidth — prefer lower operational overhead.

Goals for the POC
---
1. Validate UX latency and quality for store-assistant flows.
2. Demonstrate predictable cost per active user with initial dataset size.
3. Prove a safe data path that avoids persistent customer-sensitive data in hosted third-party storage.
4. Provide a clear migration path to Dedicated or Private if throughput/contractual needs arise.

Quick architecture options (high-level)
---
A. Hosted-first (fastest path)
- Model: Redwood hosted API using curated LLM (quantized variant where available).
- Data: API requests from client -> Redwood hosted endpoint. Send only non-sensitive context (hashed order ids); sensitive tokens redacted client-side.
- Pros: fastest to stand up, minimal infra, automatic scaling, lowest ops cost.
- Cons: data residency risk (mitigated by EU region pinning + encryption), less control over tuning/quantization.
- Cost estimate (POC): compute + token usage ~ $2.5–4k/month depending on generation frequency.
- Fit: teams prioritizing speed to demo and limited ops.

B. Dedicated-reserved (predictable throughput)
- Model: Redwood Dedicated capacity reserved in eu-west region; single tenant GPU pool sized for 40 concurrent requests with headroom.
- Topology: app -> private VPC peering -> Redwood Dedicated endpoint. KV/cache optional on customer VPC via secure tunnel.
- Pros: predictable latency, data isolation, easier to get corporate approvals. Finer control of model variants (quantized/fp16) and batching policies.
- Cons: higher monthly commitment; requires some networking setup and SRE time.
- Cost estimate (POC): base reserved capacity + usage ~ $5–8k/month (depending on commitment and burst allowance).
- Fit: customers needing control + SLA assurances with limited long-term ops team.

C. Private bridge (control-plane hosted, inference on-prem/VPC)
- Model: Customer runs inference nodes (NVIDIA A10/A30 class) in their VPC or on-prem; Redwood control plane (optionally hosted in EU) manages model versions and rollouts.
- Data: customer-originating traffic never leaves VPC; telemetry exported via metrics sink to Redwood console (scrubbed metadata only).
- Pros: maximum data control and compliance; good for regulated retail partners (payment processors, integrations); lower inference unit cost at scale.
- Cons: heavy ops footprint; model updates require coordination; POC ramp may be slower.
- Cost estimate (POC): infra + setup ~ higher up-front (>$10k one-time) but monthly infra cost could be competitive for sustained usage.
- Fit: customers with strict residency/compliance or high steady throughput.

Tradeoff table (non-numeric summary)
---
- Speed to demo: Hosted > Dedicated > Private
- Operational overhead: Hosted < Dedicated < Private
- Data control: Private > Dedicated > Hosted
- Latency predictability: Dedicated >= Private > Hosted
- POC budget friendliness: Hosted > Dedicated > Private

Practical design choices and heuristics for this customer
---
1) Start hosted with EU-region pin and strict request-side redaction. Implement telemetry hooks that mirror Redwood console events so we can compare token volumes and latency. If p95 consistently > 550ms under realistic load, escalate to Dedicated.
2) Use a 'bridge' test: provision a small Dedicated pool (short-term 1–2 week trial) to validate latency gains before committing to a longer reserved contract. This reduces risk for both sides.
3) For private/on-prem, require a minimal PoC footprint: 1x A10 equivalent for baseline, staging control-plane in EU, automated image + model sync (S3 or local registry). Don't recommend full on-prem for this initial retail POC unless legal requires it.
4) Prefab prompts and token budgets: set conservative per-request token caps (max 512) and enable prefix caching for product descriptions and FAQ contexts. This can cut token usage by ~20–35% in practice.

Telemetry and evaluative signals to capture during POC
---
- Per-route latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and model token usage.
- Session-level fidelity: divergence between baseline model and production variant on a labeled prompt set (20–50 eval prompts across common queries).
- Cost per 1k active users extrapolation.

Security and compliance checklist (POC minimums)
---
- EU-region pin for hosted; committed region for Dedicated.
- Default encryption in transit + KMS-managed keys for sensitive config/secrets.
- No persistent storage of raw PII in hosted logs: redact at edge.
- Contractual: include data processing addendum (DPA) if hosted is used.

Open questions / decisions needed
---
- How aggressive must we be on the latency SLO for the demo vs production? (ask product: demo OK if p95 < 700ms?)
- Is there any contractual prohibition on using managed hosted inference for the POC? (legal/procurement)
- Can customer accept redaction vs full private hosting for card-tokenized order ids? (security)
- Does infra want a dedicated VPC peering proof-of-concept or should we rely on hosted-region pin for the demo?

Immediate next steps (owner assignments)
---
- Asha: spin up hosted-config example, create demo key and sample telemetry dashboard (due: 2026-02-28).
- Diego: rough Dedicated cost worksheet and short-term trial plan (due: 2026-03-05).
- Priya: draft DPA talking points and legal checklist for hosted vs Dedicated (due: 2026-03-03).
- Ben: create a 20-prompt eval set reflecting retail intents and prepare a grading rubric (due: 2026-02-26).

Notes to self / meeting talking points
---
- Keep the decision criteria simple for the customer: speed, data control, and budget. Map those criteria to our three suggestions and show a clear path between them.
- Ask for a small sample of their peak traffic day (anonymized) to simulate realistic burst behavior.

Appendix — quick rough numbers (ballpark for internal planning)
---
- Hosted: expected token cost for 1k UA/day, 50k generations/month ~ $2.5k; add network+overhead ~ $500–1k.
- Dedicated (small reservation): reservation + minimal usage ~ $5k/month.
- Private minimal on-prem setup: one-time infra/setup ~ $12k, monthly infra cost variable.

End.
